name: TX-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent renominated with no outside opposition
No public polling of the race
model.rationale: The R+11 district, Ellzey's overwhelming financial advantage, and his renomination without serious opposition all point to a comfortable Republican hold, while markets price a Democratic win at only about 2%. With no polls or expert ratings to move the forecast, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly R+15 stands.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Ellzey would be the first sign of movement, but nothing currently suggests the race is competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Jake Ellzey seeks another term in a north Texas district that leans about eleven points Republican at the presidential level. He was renominated without difficulty and enters the general election with a massive financial edge, having raised roughly $4.7 million and holding $2.5 million on hand, while Democrat Danny Minton has raised only about $44,000. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money, all of which favor Ellzey heavily. Prediction markets give Democrats only a small chance of an upset. The expected result is a double-digit Republican win, with modest residual uncertainty because the race has drawn little independent attention.
